seo.title: seoPlayerTitle
seo.minimum_data: A row on a Home Top players board or on a competition page's Player rankings board — i.e. the player leads one of the four Home boards in their league's current season, or is in the top five of one of the thirteen boards of a competition-season the site carries; both are mart_leaderboards' decision (assert_mart_leaderboards_every_home_board_has_a_leader guards the Home half). That is deliberately the narrowest gate that satisfies the reason this page exists: audit-seo check 8 requires a page for every player the site links to, and those two blocks are the only pages that link to one today. It is NOT the rule for which players deserve a page — that is #845's minimum-data question, and it must stay a rule over the served mart rather than a list in the frontend.
seo.page_count_driver: count(distinct slug over landing.json .top_players[].rows[] and competitions/*/*.json .player_boards[].rows[]) x count(locales)
seo.url_permanence_note: The URL is permanent and is the one site_architecture.md section 3 already reserves for the player profile. The SLUG is {kebab-name}-{player_api_id} and still carries the id because 18.5% of provider player names collide (1.6% on the full name), so the team scheme does not transfer unchanged; moving player slugs into the warehouse the way team slugs moved is its own work (#843/#852). The id suffix is what anchors identity across a name correction. STUB: this ships the URL, its canonical, its hreflang set and a locale-distinct title, and NO content blocks. #845 owns the real Player Overview. Listed in STUB_PAGES, which blocks INDEXABLE === true until it is filled. Its inbound link is live on the day it ships, unlike the competition stub's: the Home page's Top players block is what makes this page necessary.
